questions.question: What is the biggest difference between a 'sealed class' and an 'enum class' in Kotlin?
options: An enum class cannot be used in a when expression
Subclasses of a sealed class can have multiple instances and hold their own distinct state
A sealed class does not support inheritance
An enum class can inherit from another open class
questions.explanation: Each enum constant exists only as a single instance, whereas subclasses of a sealed class can be data classes or regular classes instantiated multiple times with dynamic state.
questions.card_front: What is the biggest difference between a 'sealed class' and an 'enum class' in Kotlin?
questions.card_back: Subclasses of a sealed class can have multiple instances and hold their own distinct state

questions.question: How does the Elvis operator (?:) work in the expression `val len = name?.length ?: 0`?
options: Throws a NullPointerException if name is null
Returns the left-hand value if it is non-null; otherwise returns the default value on the right (0)
Performs an unsafe cast to Int
questions.explanation: The Elvis operator ?: returns the expression on its left if it is not null; if the left side evaluates to null, it returns the right-hand expression.
questions.card_front: How does the Elvis operator (?:) work in the expression `val len = name?.length ?: 0`?
questions.card_back: Returns the left-hand value if it is non-null; otherwise returns the default value on the right (0)

questions.question: Among Kotlin's Scope Functions, which function uses the 'this' receiver and returns the Context Object itself?
questions.explanation: apply uses 'this' as its receiver and returns the context object itself, making it ideal for object initialization and configuration.

questions.question: What is the difference between SupervisorJob() and a regular Job() in Kotlin Coroutines?
options: SupervisorJob runs twice as fast as Job
When one child coroutine fails, SupervisorJob does not cancel its sibling coroutines
SupervisorJob only runs on the Main Thread
questions.explanation: With SupervisorJob, a failure of one child coroutine does not propagate upward to cancel other sibling coroutines.
questions.card_front: What is the difference between SupervisorJob() and a regular Job() in Kotlin Coroutines?
questions.card_back: When one child coroutine fails, SupervisorJob does not cancel its sibling coroutines
